title: Case Study: Mountkirk Games — Request & Control Flow
purpose: Traces Matchmaking & Session Lifecycle Flow: player match request -> matchmaker allocation -> game server provisioning -> live gameplay -> match completion rewards.
routing_rationale: Decoupling the stateless matchmaking engine from stateful game servers allows independent scaling during sudden viral game launch surges.

nodes.label: Open Match Service
nodes.detail: Groups 100 players with similar skill rating (MMR) into match ticket.

nodes.label: Agones Allocator Service
nodes.detail: Finds Ready game pod; marks state as 'Allocated' in 15ms.

nodes.label: Active Game Session Pod
nodes.detail: Hosts multiplayer match; streams game physics updates over UDP.

nodes.label: Cloud Spanner Transaction
nodes.detail: Transacts player rewards and updates global leaderboard ranking atomically.

steps.title: Game Pod Allocation
steps.action: Open Match requests server; Agones transitions warm pod from Ready to Allocated.
steps.why_traversal: Provides instantaneous sub-second match connection for waiting players.

steps.title: Atomic Economy Finalization
steps.action: Upon victory, match rewards write to Cloud Spanner with serializable isolation.
steps.why_traversal: Eliminates cheating and virtual inventory desynchronization.

scenarios.label: Fleet Pool Depleted (All Pods Allocated)
scenarios.root_cause: Traffic spike exhausted pre-warmed Ready buffer; allocator returned 404.
scenarios.diverted_path: Matchmaking queue times increase from 2s to 45s.
scenarios.recovery: Increase Agones Fleet bufferSize to maintain 25% pre-warmed Ready pods during peak hours.

scenarios.label: Quota exhausted
scenarios.root_cause: A project or regional quota reaches its allocation limit.
scenarios.diverted_path: Requests surface elevated latency, errors, or denied actions.
